WHAT’S HAPPENING

“I’m scared to eat anything.”

Every time you eat, the number goes up. So you cut the carbs, then the bread, then the cake at every birthday. Your family watches everything on your plate. Salad for dinner, every night. And at the next checkup the number is a little higher anyway, and there’s talk of another pill.

WHAT’S REALLY GOING ON

Your insulin still works. Your cells stopped answering it.

When you eat, carbs become sugar in your blood, and insulin tells your cells to take it in and use it for energy. In 1936, Dr. Harold Himsworth found that many adults with high blood sugar had plenty of insulin. Their cells had simply stopped responding to it. In 1988, Dr. Gerald Reaven gave it a name: insulin resistance.

That’s why cutting food only goes so far. It lowers how much sugar goes in. It doesn’t help your cells respond to the sugar that’s already there.

The 7 mistakes, and what actually helps

Salad every night?

1

Mistake: Thinking the answer is always to eat less

Before 1922, people with high blood sugar were put on near-starvation diets. A century later, most advice still comes down to the same thing: eat less. But less food doesn’t fix cells that aren’t answering insulin.

What changes: You can eat a real dinner again. Resilia’s 1,000 mg of true Ceylon cinnamon helps your cells respond to insulin and supports healthy glucose metabolism, so your body handles the food you eat instead of you having to fear it.†

Exhausted an hour after eating?

2

Mistake: Treating it like a willpower problem

When your cells don’t let sugar in, they run short on fuel even with plenty of it in your blood. That’s the after-meal slump, and the cravings that hit hardest at night. It was never willpower.

What changes: No more couch after every meal. Berberine HCl (500 mg) supports cellular energy production, so your cells turn food into fuel. Many people notice steadier energy after meals and fewer late-night cravings.†*

Mistake: Turning every meal into a fight

Saying no at every birthday. Checking before every meal. Everyone watching what you put on your plate. It wears you down, and it still doesn’t touch what’s happening in your cells.

What changes: You get to sit at the table again. Two capsules with breakfast give your body daily support for healthy blood sugar levels already within the normal range, so meals stop being a fight and birthdays stop being a test.†

“Cinnamon? That’s a spice.”

4

Mistake: Thinking natural means weak

Natural doesn’t mean weak. Researchers in Sri Lanka have studied true Ceylon cinnamon in adults with high blood sugar, and berberine has been studied in dozens of controlled human trials on blood sugar.

What changes: You get two clinically studied ingredients working together. Ceylon cinnamon (1,000 mg) helps the doors open; berberine (500 mg) helps flip the switch from storing to burning. Two pathways, one capsule routine.†

Already have cinnamon in the cupboard?

5

Mistake: Thinking all cinnamon is the same

Go look. If it’s one thick, hard roll of bark, that’s cassia, a different tree, and it’s most of the cinnamon sold in America. True Ceylon is thin and papery, with layers rolled inside each other. Cassia is so high in coumarin that Europe limits how much can go into food. Ceylon has about 250 times less.

What changes: You finally get the cinnamon the research is about. Resilia uses only true Ceylon (Cinnamomum verum) bark extract, standardized to cinnamaldehyde and polyphenols. Safe to take every day, never cassia.†

Mistake: Thinking it has to be complicated

“I take five pills, I check my sugar three times a day, and I count every carb. I can’t remember one more thing.” You don’t have to.
